title: Lumenary CS
subtitle: Computer science from a first program to the frontier of AI: algorithms, systems, software at scale, machine learning and how large models are built.
description: Lumenary CS is the second subject of Lumenary Scientia, free and open source like Lumenary Math. It starts with no experience at all and climbs, lesson by lesson, through data structures, algorithms and computer systems to the engineering practised at the largest technology companies and the research done at AI labs today.

Every lesson teaches with ideas first and code second. Code is in Python, and every block with a **Run in browser** button runs there, in a sandbox, with nothing to install. The runnable examples and the Python exercises are run by Lumenary's test suite, and a lesson says *Code tested* only when all of its code passed.

Every lesson was drafted with AI assistance and is awaiting review by a human computer scientist. The text, exercises and code are original and licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (code Apache-2.0). Where a lab, company or project has published the primary source — a paper, a design document, an engineering blog — the lesson links to it rather than retelling it.

levels.title: First programs
levels.summary: No experience needed, from about age 11. What a computer actually does, and your first programs in Python: values, decisions, loops, functions and collections, and how to find and fix mistakes.

levels.title: Data structures and the cost of computation
levels.summary: How to measure what a program costs, and the structures every programmer reaches for: arrays and lists, stacks and queues, hash tables, trees, heaps and graphs.

levels.title: Algorithm design
levels.summary: The design techniques behind fast programs, from greedy choices and dynamic programming to shortest paths, string matching and randomness, and what to do when a problem is provably hard.

levels.title: How computers work
levels.summary: Down through the layers: how data is encoded in bits, how logic gates become a processor, why memory has a hierarchy, what an operating system does, and how concurrency, networks, databases and compilers work.

levels.title: Building software that lasts
levels.summary: How professional software is built: version control, testing, design and types, security and applied cryptography.

levels.title: Systems at scale
levels.summary: The engineering of large services: distributed systems, replication and consensus, storage at scale, batch and stream processing, system design, reliability, and how to show all of it in a technical interview.

levels.title: Machine learning
levels.summary: Learning from data, from linear models and gradient descent to neural networks you build and train yourself, and the architectures that led to the transformer.

levels.title: The frontier of AI
levels.summary: How today's large models are built, trained, served, evaluated, understood and made safe: the working knowledge of an AI lab in 2026, with links to the labs' own papers and documentation.
